fields.title: Single source of truth
fields.keyTakeaway: A source of truth is assigned by attribute, not by system, and relies on an explicitly named owner.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A client's phone number exists in the product, the CRM, the support system, email campaigns, and the call center export. It differs across them. Who is right?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: The lack of an assigned source of truth costs not so much in errors as in time: every argument about a figure or attribute starts over, and the same people participate every time. In total, this amounts to weeks per year for a team that could have been working on the product.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: A [[source-of-truth|source of truth]] is a system whose value is considered correct when discrepancies arise. The key word is "considered": this is an assigned agreement, not a property of the data.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Every entity has one source, not every system.** Not "CRM is right about everything," but "phone number is source product, client segment is source CRM, contract status is source billing." Breakdown by attribute, not by system, because each system knows best about its own domain.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **The source has a [[data-owner|owner]]—a person or role.** They decide what the attribute means, who can change it, and what to do in case of conflict. Without an owner, the agreement falls apart in a quarter.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Other systems receive a copy and do not edit it.** As soon as a second system starts writing to the same attribute, there are two sources, and everything returns to square one.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: A separate task is the [[golden-record|golden record]]: consolidating data about a single object from multiple systems. It boils down to [[entity-resolution|entity resolution]]—determining that two records describe the same person. A single client has two accounts with different phones; is this one person or two? The answer is a product answer and has consequences for analytics, mailings, and support.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Data about a partner store lived in three places: product, CRM, accounting. Store names diverged in 12% of cases, legal details in 4%. The partner dashboard showed one thing, the contract contained another.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Splitting names into two attributes removed the bulk of discrepancies: it turned out they weren't arguing about the value, but about what to call the name. "Romashka" store for the customer and "Romashka-Torg LLC" in the contract were two different facts that people had spent a year trying to cram into a single field.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: The agreement only works if synchronization is implemented. An assigned source without a data flow is just a document, and discrepancies continue—only now with the feeling that the issue has been resolved.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: A source of truth is assigned by attribute, not by system, and relies on an explicitly named owner.
